taxonomy:
## Taxonomy of grid-based logic games (from the provided rules only)

### A. Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black squares/frame; bulbs can’t illuminate each other; each white cell must be illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color some cells black so numbered cells count white cells to nearest black or frame (horizontally + vertically); numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.
- **Heyawake**: In bold-bordered rooms, numbers give count of painted cells; white cells can’t stretch across more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.

### B. Loop / path drawing (single closed loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers; must pass all white-circle cells with area-wise straight-through or right-angled turns; must not pass black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through all circle cells; white circles require straight-through with a right-angled turn in adjacent cell(s); black circles require a right-angled turn then straight through next cell.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; must pass arrow cells; wind direction blocks movement against wind; special side-wind bending constraints.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop; must pass all black circles with the circle as midpoint of the straight segment through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; each bold-bordered room visited exactly once; in each room loop passes either all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); alternates moon-room then sun-room behavior.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through all “gates” (dotted segments); each gate passed once; loop starts/returns to open numbered circle; gate numbers constrain crossing order relative to start.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop; must not pass through black cells or numbered cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Slitherlink**: Single loop through dots; numbers indicate how many line segments surround the cell; empty cells unconstrained; loop never crosses/branches.
- **Yosenabe**: Not a loop, but movement-based; included separately under “movement” (see F).

### C. Region partitioning / tiling with shape or count rules
- **Chained Block**: Partition into “blocks” of consecutive black cells; each block has one number or “?”; blocks form chains via corner contact; no two blocks in a chain share the same size/shape (up to rotation/mirror).
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines; each block contains two areas (white + gray) of same form (rotation/mirror allowed); block number equals half the total cells of that color in the block.
- **Evolomino**: Fill board with numbers by blocks; each block has size equal to its number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Five Cells**: Divide into blocks of exactly five cells; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell (including outer frame); lines can’t enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill empty cells with numbers; each block has uniform number and size equals that number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges; number of bridges equals island number; max two bridges between islands; bridges can’t cross islands/bridges; all islands connected.
- **Nurimeizu**: Shaded/unshaded regions with bold outlines; each outlined region contains exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are connected orthogonally; blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded group.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade some cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of same number; blocks connected orthogonally; blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its area (cell count).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered “Tiles”; color tiles so that diagonal-line numbers constrain count of black cells to the right/down along the diagonal’s line/column until grid edge or another diagonal-number cell; all cells in a tile are either all colored or all uncolored.
- **Sto-stone**: Bold-bordered “Rooms”; number in room gives count of continuous black cells; rooms with no number unconstrained; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; after dropping stones straight down, stones must fill bottom half with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Ripple Effect**: Bold-bordered “Rooms”; fill empty cells with consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicates in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ that number.
- **Sashigane**: Divide into L-shaped blocks (one cell wide); all blocks must be L-shaped; open circles mark the “knee” (bend); open-circle numbers give block cell count; arrow marks one end pointing toward the knee; total marks per block is 0–3.
- **Satogaeri**: Bold-bordered “Countries”; move circles orthogonally so each country has exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; some circles without numbers may be immobile; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Choco Banana**: (From rules) paint some cells black so black orthogonally-connected cells form rectangles/squares; white orthogonally-connected cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate size of the area containing the cell.

### D. Coloring / shading / black-white placement with connectivity
- **Choco Banana**: Black cells orthogonally connected must form rectangle/square; white cells orthogonally connected must not form rectangle/square; numbers give area size.
- **Hitori**: Color cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Kurodoko**: (also fits A) black cells can’t touch orthogonally; numbered cells stay white; all white cells connected.
- **Nurikabe**: Fill with black wall cells and white areas; numbers give count of continuous white cells; each white area has exactly one number; black cells form continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nuritwin**: (also fits C) shaded blocks in outlined regions; connectivity and non-touching constraints; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; cells with numbers cannot be colored; (additional constraints appear in the provided text for this game: colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells; and each rectangle has exactly one wrong number—see below).
- **Usowan** (continued from provided rules): number next to a cell counts colored neighbors orthogonally; in each bold-bordered rectangle there is exactly one wrong number; colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares (not in black squares); uncovered white cells must form rectangle/square; numbers indicate how many black triangles are around it orthogonally.
- **Yajilin**: (also fits B) loop-based but includes black-cell constraints: black cells can’t touch orthogonally and loop avoids black/number cells.

### E. Snake / ordered path constraints (non-loop or sequential entities)
- **Hebi**: Place numbers in squares so figures 1→5 are sequentially connected in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; from 2→1 direction, other snakes can’t appear in the next squares up to the next black square/frame (attack rule); black squares’ numbers indicate nearest snake distance in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Nagareru**: (also fits B) loop with wind direction; arrows constrain movement against wind.

### F. Movement / routing of tokens (not necessarily loops)
- **Satogaeri**: Move circles within bold “countries” with orthogonal motion; each country ends with exactly one circle; circle numbers constrain pass-through cell count; circles can’t cross tracks or other circles.
- **Yosenabe**: Move all circles orthogonally into gray areas; each move shown by straight arrow whose tip is in a gray cell; arrows don’t bend or cross other circles/arrows; number in a gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it; empty gray areas unconstrained but at least one circle must enter some gray area.

### G. Pairing / connection without crossing (paths)
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of equal numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally or with turns; lines can’t cross/branch; lines can’t go through numbered cells.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (also fits C) bridges connect islands; continuous link between all islands.

### H. Arithmetic / constraint satisfaction on fixed grid (Sudoku-like)
- **Sudoku**: Place numbers 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each 3×3 bold block contains all numbers 1–9.

### I. Arrow / pencil / directional segment constraints
- **Pencils**: Identify “pencils” as straight groups of cells with a tip at one end; pencil line passes through cell centers orthogonally or turning; numbers in pencil cells give pencil length; line from tip must go through as many cells as the number; pencil line can’t self-cross or branch.
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with numbers from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; each cell has only one digit.
- **Yajilin**: (also fits B) arrow direction is not present; included earlier under loop constraints.

### J. Local adjacency / uniqueness constraints (no region partitioning)
- **Akari**: (also fits A) bulbs illuminate orthogonally until black/frame; every white cell illuminated; bulbs can’t illuminate each other.
- **Hitori**: uniqueness of numbers in rows/columns; black cells non-touching; white connected.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-enclosed territories have numbers indicating how many more of the marks they get; “—” extends across >3 cells horizontally but ≤2 vertically; “|” extends across >3 cells vertically but ≤2 horizontally.
- **Kurotto**: Color cells with circles fixed; circle number equals sum of continuous black cells extending vertically and horizontally from it; empty circles can have any number; circle cells can’t be colored.
- **Nurikabe**: (also fits D) numbers constrain continuous white cell counts; black wall connectivity and 2×2 prohibition.

### K. Rectangle/shape formation constraints (orthogonal geometry)
- **Choco Banana**: black orthogonally-connected components must be rectangles/squares; white components must not be rectangles/squares.
- **Heyawake**: white cells can’t stretch across more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells not separated by painted cells.
- **Shakashaka**: uncovered white cells form rectangle/square.
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**: forbid 2×2 fully shaded groups; blocks connected orthogonally.
